 Yemen's Houthis call for immediate evacuation of Aden airport
 Wednesday, 28 Oct 2026
 | 7:25 PM MYT
 share 
 bookmark 
 FILE PHOTO: Passengers at Aden Airport in Aden, Yemen January 1, 2026. REUTERS/Fawaz Salman/ File Photo 
 DUBAI/ADEN, Oct ⁠28 (Reuters) - Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis ⁠on Wednesday called on people ‌to evacuate immediately from the international airport in Aden, where the internationally ​recognised, Saudi-backed government is ⁠based.
 Houthi spokesperson Yahya ⁠Saree said in his post ⁠on X ‌that the evacuation was due to ⁠what he said was the presence ​there ‌of a Saudi military cargo ⁠aircraft carrying ​weapons. There was no immediate comment from Saudi authorities. 
 The ⁠Houthi militia, which controls ​the capital Sanaa in the north, has repeatedly struck the airport, ⁠a humanitarian lifeline and gateway for southern Yemen.
 Explosions were heard in Aden before the Houthi ​warning, residents in ⁠the city told Reuters. 
 (Reporting by ​Nayera Abdallah, Mohammed ‌Ghobari, Reyam Mokhashef; ​Writing by Muhammad Al Gebaly; Editing by Andrew Heavens)
